{{Other uses|H-matrix (disambiguation){{!}}H-matrix}}
{{expert needed|mathematics|reason=to review the article|date=July 2018}}
In mathematics, an '''''H''-matrix''' is a [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] whose [[comparison matrix]] is an [[M-matrix]]. It is useful in [[iterative method]]s.

'''Definition:''' Let {{math|1=''A'' = (''a<sub>ij</sub>'')}} be a {{math|''n'' × ''n''}} complex matrix. Then [[comparison matrix]] ''M''(''A'') of complex matrix ''A'' is defined as {{math|1=''M''(''A'') = ''α''<sub>''ij''</sub>}} where {{math|1=''α''<sub>''ij''</sub> = −{{!}}''A''<sub>''ij''</sub>{{!}}}} for all {{math|1=''i'' ≠ ''j'', 1 ≤ ''i,j'' ≤ ''n''}} and {{math|1=''α<sub>ij</sub>'' = {{!}}''A<sub>ij</sub>''{{!}}}} for all {{math|1=''i'' = ''j'', 1 ≤ ''i,j'' ≤ ''n''}}. If ''M''(''A'') is a [[M-matrix]], ''A'' is a ''H''-matrix.

[[Invertible matrix|Invertible]] H-matrix guarantees convergence of [[Gauss–Seidel method|Gauss–Seidel iterative methods]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Zhang |first1= Cheng-yi |last2= Ye |first2= Dan |last3= Zhong |first3= Cong-Lei |last4= SHUANGHUA |first4= SHUANGHUA |year=2015 |title= Convergence on Gauss–Seidel iterative methods for linear systems with general H-matrices |journal=The Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra |volume=30 |pages=843–870 |doi=10.13001/1081-3810.1972 |url=http://repository.uwyo.edu/ela/vol30/iss1/54/ |accessdate=21 June 2018 |arxiv= 1410.3196 }}</ref>
